ref_text: As a simulation tool, Biffrost is a co simulation

lines.text: A ninety-nine dollar board from twenty twelve wrote this.
It's a Parallella. One chip with sixteen cores, each holding thirty-two kilobytes. Half a megabyte in all.
A small story model has fifteen million weights: sixty megabytes. It cannot fit, so the weights stream in for every word.
So the model was trained with three values per weight: minus one, zero and one. Sixteen times smaller, and it still writes.
Every multiply runs on that chip. Checked word for word against a reference: identical.
So it runs. How fast? On paper, sixty tokens a second.
The board's own ARM processor, for comparison, manages fourteen.
Measured on the chip: forty-nine. The cause was the transfer size. One-kilobyte chunks: fifty-nine.
But that was one matrix pass, not the model. The whole model runs at just under sixteen.
Batching shares the weights. Eight stories at once: forty. Two boards: eighty. Each story still waits a fifth of a second per token.
Sixty was true, for a matrix pass. Measure the thing you ship.
